clue.text: Mo is a rascal concocting hair dressing

indicators.note: concocting means cooking up or mixing, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A roguish man named Mo whips up his own hair product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocting' shuffles the eleven letters of MO IS A RASCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Macassar oil was a popular Victorian pomade, an oily preparation men put on their hair.

clue.text: Relentless advance of harridan supporting a month of hype

indicators.note: supporting in a down entry means holding up from below, so the harridan piece goes last

parts.note: March is a month
taken as written
PR, public relations, is promotional hype
an ogress is a fearsome woman, a harridan

explanation.surface: A shrew backs a month of publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a month' is not a length of time here; it is the month's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: The march of progress is an idiom for steady, unstoppable advancement.

clue.text: Company adopts style that's capital

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the style word goes inside

parts.note: an air is a manner or style

explanation.surface: A firm takes on a fashionable look that is first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Girl lived under speakeasy

indicators.note: under means this piece sits below the other in the down entry

parts.note: she refers to a girl
been means existed or lived

explanation.surface: A girl lived beneath an illicit bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, the Irish equivalent of a speakeasy.

clue.text: Joiner takes venture fairly slowly

parts.note: and is a conjunction, a joining word
to ante is to put up a stake, to venture money

explanation.surface: A carpenter takes a gamble at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' looks like a carpenter but means a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical direction for a moderately slow, walking tempo.

clue.text: Empty-headed boy hides Rover in the greenhouse

indicators.note: hides means holds out of sight inside
empty-headed means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its head
a ranger is a rover, one who roams

explanation.surface: A dim lad is concealing a dog called Rover among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' looks like a dog's name, but here it means a wanderer; 'Empty-headed' leaves OY, and 'hides' wraps it round the rover word.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glasshouse originally built to grow orange trees.

clue.text: The unemployed lied wildly about certain Tory women

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the next piece
wildly signals that the letters of lied are thrown about

parts.note: sure means certain
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
lasses are young women

explanation.surface: Idle people told reckless lies about some Conservative ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' gives LEID, and 'about' wraps it round the certain word; 'unemployed' is a playful take on those who never need to work.
explanation.definitionFit: The leisured classes are people who need not work, which is ironically called being unemployed.

clue.text: Bad writing makes Bob cringe

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated S
to crawl is to cringe or grovel

explanation.surface: Poor handwriting makes someone named Bob wince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is a pre-decimal British shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is hasty, untidy handwriting.

clue.text: The way a good man catches a plane, for example

indicators.note: catches means holds within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
a plane is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: A virtuous man boards an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the plane tree, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, a public way through a town.

clue.text: Red truck beside quarry

parts.note: in the US a car can be a railway truck or wagon; here simply a vehicle
a quarry is a pit where stone is dug, like a mine

explanation.surface: A red lorry is parked next to a stone pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson shade, so it names a kind of red.

clue.text: Little girl with sitar stirred writer

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so the letters of sitar are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small girl plays a jumbled sitar for an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist is a person who writes a diary, so a kind of writer.

clue.text: Remains an outside agent for museum

indicators.note: outside means the first pieces are placed around the agent word

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
taken as written
a mole is a spy or secret agent planted in an organisation

explanation.surface: Leftover bits sit outside a spy's hideout near a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent' is a spy here, not a salesman; 'outside' puts the remains and 'an' on either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean in Oxford is a famous university museum of art and archaeology.

clue.text: Contemplate stocking superior dressing

indicators.note: stocking here means holding inside, as a shop stocks goods, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to contemplate is to gaze at something
U is the abbreviation for upper-class or superior

explanation.surface: Someone muses over hosiery and a top-quality bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like hosiery but means containing: GAZE holds U. U for upper-class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauze is the thin open fabric used as a medical dressing on wounds.

clue.text: Fellow hides in many an attic

indicators.note: hides in means the fellow letter is tucked inside the following word

parts.note: a lot means many
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A man is concealed in many a roof space.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is the space under a roof, the same room as an attic.

clue.text: Stop and notice people getting tons of affection

parts.note: to end something is to stop it
to give ear is to take notice or pay attention
men are people

explanation.surface: Halt and observe folk receiving loads of warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: An endearment is a word or gesture expressing affection, so the definition names what it shows.

clue.text: Erudite student to recite

parts.note: L is a learner driver, a student
to iterate is to repeat or recite

explanation.surface: A scholarly student is told to say lines aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Being literate means well read and educated, which is erudite.

clue.text: Man gets wind of betting system

parts.note: Martin is a man's name
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A man gets a whisper of a gambling scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind of' reads as a hint or rumour, but 'wind' is a strong blow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A martingale is a gambling system of doubling the stake after each loss.

clue.text: Miss fellow catching fish

indicators.note: catching means taking hold inside

parts.note: a man is a fellow
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A young woman's boyfriend lands a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an unmarried young woman, a miss.

clue.text: Try getting wife to contribute equally

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
dutch, from old dutch, is Cockney slang for a wife

explanation.surface: Have a shot at persuading your spouse to share the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' for wife is Cockney, from 'my old Dutch'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each person paying their own share.

clue.text: Both queen and barbarian, when put up, like thin plates

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means read from bottom to top

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
an animal is a brutish barbarian

explanation.surface: Both a monarch and a savage, raised up, resemble slim sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when put up' turns RANIMAL upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminar means arranged in or consisting of thin layers or plates.

clue.text: Head of stable clipped tail

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from stable

parts.note: clipped means cut

explanation.surface: A stable manager has given a horse a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Agreement for attempt to catch swallow

indicators.note: to catch means to hold within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to eat is to swallow food

explanation.surface: A deal is struck for a bid to net a swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like the bird but is the verb for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: One does not start a fire

indicators.note: does not start means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: Someone fails to light a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' means SINGLE; 'does not start' drops its first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an old word for a fire on a domestic hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Establish escort eats whipped cream

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a date is a companion or escort for an outing

indicators.note: whipped means beaten, so the letters of cream are churned up

explanation.surface: A companion tucks into some whipped cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escort' as a date is a companion for an evening; 'whipped' gives EMARC and 'eats' puts it within the companion word.
explanation.definitionFit: To demarcate is to set or establish the limits or boundary of something.

clue.text: "Lift the beams", we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the clue word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to hoist the timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' suggests timber, but it means rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up.

clue.text: English worker keeps on being stylish

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the next word is held within

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker, from worker ants
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: An English labourer keeps on being fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps on' reads as a phrase, but 'on' is LEG: in cricket the on side and leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, which is stylish.

clue.text: Punch hurts during capture

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to net is to capture
ails means troubles or hurts

explanation.surface: A blow lands, causing pain while someone is being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail set is a punch-like tool used to drive nail heads below a surface.

clue.text: Amaryllis dresses badly without trendy husband

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters go around the other pieces
badly signals that the letters of dresses are jumbled

parts.note: hep is old slang for trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: A flower-named woman dresses poorly with no fashionable spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: SERDESS (from 'dresses', jumbled by 'badly') wraps round HEP and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaryllis is a stock name for a shepherd girl in pastoral poetry from Virgil and Theocritus.
